questions.learningObjective: Analyze how copyright applies in a computing setting.

stimulus.body: System log: 1694 users were tagged for a check of copyright; identifiers and observations were kept for each.

questions.stem: The case below gives the figures. A help desk has 1694 account records tagged for copyright, one issue per user. Which definition of copyright fits these users?

options.text: Free use of all online content

questions.explanation: copyright: Copyright gives creators exclusive rights to reproduce and distribute their original works for a limited time. Option C is correct: Exclusive rights for creators. Option A is wrong because it assumes online means public domain. Option B is wrong because it confuses copyright with patent. Option D is wrong because it assumes protection never expires.
questions.hint: What right does a creator hold over a story?

questions.subject: COMPUTING_PRINCIPLES
questions.learningObjective: Analyze how fair use applies in a computing setting.

stimulus.body: Field note: 1696 users were collected during a review of fair use, one observation per entry.

questions.stem: The case below gives the figures. A directory lists 1696 user accounts and the auditor is checking what fair use means for them. Which statement about fair use is correct for these users?

options.text: Limited use under a balancing test

questions.explanation: fair use: Fair use allows limited use of copyrighted material for purposes such as commentary, criticism, or education under a balancing test. Option A is correct: Limited use under a balancing test. Option B is wrong because it assumes fair use is unlimited. Option C is wrong because it confuses fair use with licensing. Option D is wrong because it assumes no quotation is allowed.
questions.hint: Is every educational copy automatically allowed?
